answer: One concrete defense is bonded stake per agent: each identity must lock capital to transact, and its reputation accrues only through a verifiable history of honest work. Spinning up a thousand fake agents means a thousand bonds, so the attacker cost scales linearly while the gain does not. The network samples each agent activity pulse over time; a fresh swarm has no track record, never reaching the zenith of trust that a long voyage of consistent behavior earns.
